about.title: About
paragraphs: I'm in my final year of school (11th grade) and applying to university in Vienna. I launched my first project in Turkey: evening open-air film screenings at a café.
In Russia I launched two projects of my own, Trajectory and Teya, and worked as a product manager at an EdTech startup. I've run more than 200 user interviews.
I lead teams from the inside: I understand almost every part of a startup, from customer discovery to code. Right now I'm looking for my niche.

facts.v: Russian, English, Tatar, Turkish, Japanese, German

items.name: Trajectory
items.task: Connect a student, their parents, companies and universities through a “Digital DNA” — a living profile of interests, skills and strengths.
items.did: The idea, customer discovery and all the engineering. I built the team and pitched the project at Startup Village 2026.
items.result: 6 written cooperation agreements with schools, companies and a senator.

items.name: Teya
items.tag: My own project · AI for psychologists
items.task: After a session, a psychologist needs to record and make sense of the case quickly.
items.did: I ran in-depth interviews with psychologists and launched the product: the psychologist dictates their thoughts, and Teya turns them into a structured note and a running case memory.

items.name: Bakir OS
items.task: Keep ideas, finances, projects and messages in one place without losing context.
items.did: I built a Telegram bot on Claude with a set of tools: it records ideas, tracks finances, transcribes voice messages, finds olympiads and grants, and remembers project context. The bot decides which tool to call.
items.result: Running 24/7 since April 2026. I'm its user and its developer.

items.name: Foundation Lab
items.did: I ran the AI tutor and the AI personal-brand projects: user interviews, hypotheses, launch.

items.name: Websites for small businesses

items.result: Three live demos — open them and check.

ai.title: How I work with AI
ai.lead: A site is built not by one prompt but by four agents in turn. Each one checks the one before.

steps.name: Audit
steps.text: Finds what gets in the customer's way on the old site.
steps.log: Auditor: tiny text, three buttons, no offer.

steps.name: Copy
steps.text: Writes one offer and one button — from verified facts.

steps.name: Build
steps.text: Assembles the page: phone first, fast, nothing extra.

steps.name: Critique
steps.text: Looks with the customer's eyes and sends it back for fixes.
steps.log: Critic: offer visible, one button, readable.

ai.idle: Press it and watch the site come together.
ai.mockCaption: An illustrative example, not a real client.
ai.note: I accept the site myself, on a phone: an agent saying “done” is not sign-off.
